text: Could you send me that in writing?
If you can move us tonight, we will take it.
Unless you cover the taxi, we will have to pay for it ourselves.
We will book somewhere ourselves if we do not hear anything by six.
If that is everything you can authorise, could you ask a supervisor?
We have a confirmed reservation. What can you offer us tonight?

I answer consumer complaints for a living, and people always ask me the same thing. When should I ask for a supervisor? My answer is: later than you think, and earlier than never. The person at the desk has a list of things they are allowed to authorise, and that list is short. It is not that they do not want to help you. They physically cannot. So the first question is not can I speak to a manager. The first question is: what are you able to offer me yourself? If the answer covers your problem, you are finished in two minutes. If it does not, then you say it plainly: if that is everything you can authorise, could you ask a supervisor? That sentence is not aggressive. It tells the person in front of you that you understand their limit, and it moves the case up without making an enemy. And one more thing, which is the piece almost nobody does. Ask for it in writing. Not because you plan to go to court, but because a company that has written something down remembers it.

I was a duty supervisor at an airport for nine years, so let me tell you what actually happened on my side of the desk. When a passenger came to me, I already knew the problem. What I did not know was what would satisfy them, and that is the thing they almost never said. Somebody would talk for four minutes about how long they had waited, and I still had no idea what I was supposed to do. The passengers who got the most were the ones who finished with a sentence like this: if you can get us on the morning flight, we will take it; if you cannot, we will need a hotel and dinner tonight. Two options, both reasonable, and now I am choosing instead of guessing. Unless the request was impossible, I gave them one of the two, and I did it fast, because there were forty people behind them. And the passenger who only said this is unacceptable got nothing, every single time, because there was nothing for me to say yes to.
If you can move us to another hotel tonight, we will take it.
